question: A coordinate model represents three consecutive vertices of a parallelogram by $A(1,2,-1)$, $B(4,-1,2)$ and $C(6,3,1)$. The fourth vertex is denoted by $D$. Students use the relation between the position vectors of consecutive vertices to locate $D$. They then compare the component vectors of the opposite sides and examine the points dividing both diagonals in the ratio $1:1$.(a) Write the position vectors of $A$, $B$ and $C$.(b) Determine the position vector and coordinates of $D$.(c) Verify that the corresponding opposite-side vectors are equal.(d) Show using the section formula that the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ have the same midpoint.
explanation: (a)The position vectors are`\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}`and`\vec{c}=6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}`(b)For consecutive vertices of a parallelogram,`\vec{a}+\vec{c}=\vec{b}+\vec{d}`Therefore,`\vec{d}=\vec{a}+\vec{c}-\vec{b}\vec{d}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})+(6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k})-(4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\vec{d}=3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}`Hence, $D=(3,6,-2)$.(c)`\overrightarrow{AB}=\vec{b}-\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\overrightarrow{DC}=\vec{c}-\vec{d}=3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}`Thus, $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{DC}$. Also,`\overrightarrow{BC}=\vec{c}-\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{k}\overrightarrow{AD}=\vec{d}-\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{k}`Thus, $\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AD}$.(d)The position vector of the midpoint of $AC$ is`\frac{\vec{a}+\vec{c}}{2}=\frac{7}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{j}`The position vector of the midpoint of $BD$ is`\frac{\vec{b}+\vec{d}}{2}=\frac{7}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{j}`Hence, the diagonals have the same midpoint and bisect each other.

options.A:
(a) $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
(b) $\vec{d}=3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$, so $D=(3,6,-2)$
(c) $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{DC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AD}$
(d) Both diagonals have midpoint position vector $\frac{7}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{j}$
options.B:
(a) $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
(b) $D=(9,0,2)$
(c) Opposite sides have opposite component vectors
(d) The midpoint of $AC$ is $\frac{7}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{j}$ but differs from that of $BD$
options.C:
(a) $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
(b) $D=(3,6,2)$
(c) $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{CD}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{DA}$
(d) The diagonals have different midpoints
options.D:
(a) $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
(b) $D=(3,4,-2)$
(c) Only one pair of opposite sides is equal
(d) The midpoint of $AC$ is $\frac{5}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{7}{2}\hat{j}$
